implemented: Linux native Claude and Codex launch through one per-profile registry, including configured instances, discovery and quota probes.
Lazy systemd scope discovery, legacy OOMPolicy fallback, owned-profile orphan cleanup and upstream memory, CPU, IO and task limits.
Child OOM score 800 without a shell wrapper; native arguments, environment changes, cwd, stdio and process ownership are retained.
Shared Codex scopes use OOMPolicy=continue when available; legacy shared scopes retain OOM diagnostics and cannot be killed for one thread. Joining another session clears stale scope ownership.

Bounded thread tracking, delayed and sticky OOM diagnosis, scope-stop guards, cgroup.kill with awaited writes and systemctl kill fallback. Explicit adapter shutdown awaits scope cleanup; dropped scopes schedule best-effort cleanup.
Confirmed OOM replaces generic transport EOF text in the run visible to the compatible client. Claude descendants inherit the trusted app thread ID.

Server browsers use the same profile registry with unowned collecting scopes, preserve CDP descriptors 3/4, and await scope cleanup on actor exit. File descriptors are owned on every launch error/cancellation path.

nativeSystemdChecks: Detached setsid descendants are reaped after their parent exits.
Per-thread cgroup.kill terminates the owned parent and detached descendant.
Shared processes survive a per-thread kill request.
An asserted 32 MiB kernel memory.max causes a confirmed, sticky OOM result.
Restarted profile cleanup stops only that profile; another profile remains running.
CDP pipes survive the real systemd wrapper; browser OOM score and owned slice match, another tab survives a sibling close, and final shutdown reaps the process.
